traditions.label: Lübeck Diocesan Use (Missale Lubicense)
traditions.scope: Printed diocesan Mass-book witnesses attributed to the Diocese of Lübeck (1486–c. 1505).
traditions.coverage_note: Documents the inspected c. 1505 Usuarium 7238 witness and records the 1486 Matthäus Brandis incunable (Usuarium 41 / ISTC im00659300) as a provisional lead; USTC 741258/676212 reconciliation and Reformation closure remain open.

traditions.label: Merseburg Diocesan Use (Missale Merseburgense)

traditions.label: Benedictine Monastic Missals (Missale Benedictinum / Casinense / Romano-Monasticum)
traditions.scope: Selected non-Bursfelde, non-Cluniac Benedictine printed missal states (1481 generic Benedictine incunable, 1580 Cassinese Congregation missal, 1937 Missale Romano-Monasticum rubric extract); kept distinct from individual abbey uses, Bursfelde, and Cluny.
traditions.coverage_note: Documents three bounded printed/preliminary states without asserting a single unified Benedictine recension across independent congregations.

stages.limitations: Catalogue metadata only; incipit is not verified as an episcopal promulgation act and original body text is uninspected.
stages.reception: Bibliographic witness only.

stages.label: 1256 Humbert of Romans prototype & portable master exemplar
stages.date_label: 1255–1263 (1256 chapter revision; portable exemplar BL Add. MS 23935)
stages.scope: Mid-13th-century standardized Dominican liturgical archetype (Santa Sabina XIV L 1) and Master General portable exemplar (BL Add. MS 23935).
stages.witness_label: Arch. OP Roma XIV L 1 (1256) & British Library Add. MS 23935 (1255–1263)
stages.summary: Inspected scholarship (O'Carroll 1979) documents the 1256 Humbert of Romans chapter standardization across fourteen complementary liturgical books and compares the Temporal pericopes of BL Add. MS 23935 with Santa Sabina XIV L 1.

evidence.claim: Dates BL Add. MS 23935 to 1255–1263 and establishes the 1256 prototype structure and Temporal pericope agreement.
Identifies the 1256 Ordinary of the Roman Correctorium at Arch. OP Roma.

stages.limitations: Pericope agreement does not prove total textual identity across all fourteen books of the prototype and portable exemplar; later additions exist in BL Add. MS 23935.
stages.reception: Order-wide normative prototype promulgated by the 1256 General Chapter; actual province-by-province conformity took decades.

stages.label: 1482 Venice Dominican incunable missal (Octavianus Scotus)
stages.scope: Earliest dated printed Dominican missal (Venice: Octavianus Scotus).
stages.witness_label: Missale secundum ordinem Fratrum Praedicatorum (Venice: Octavianus Scotus, 24 December 1482)
stages.summary: ISTC im00636000 / GW M24176 documents Octavianus Scotus's 24 December 1482 Venetian printing of the Dominican missal, predating Nicolaus de Frankfordia's 1484 Venice printing.

evidence.claim: Identifies the 24 December 1482 Venice Scotus Dominican missal.

stages.limitations: Provisional lead; original incunable scan not yet inspected or collated against 1484 and 1550.
stages.reception: Publication lead only.

stages.label: 1484 Venice Dominican incunable missal (Nicolaus de Frankfordia)
stages.scope: Early Venetian printed Dominican missal held in the repository act-history catalogue.
stages.witness_label: Incipit missale secundum Ordinem Fratrum Predicatorum (Venice: Nicolaus de Frankfordia, 1484)
stages.summary: Digitized Boston Public Library copy (598 images) verifies the 1484 Venetian printing of the Dominican missal prior to the 1550 Giunta edition.

evidence.claim: Verifies the 1484 Venice Nicolaus de Frankfordia Dominican missal (598 images).

stages.limitations: Opening incipit and imprint verified; body text uncollated against 1256 prototype or 1550 Giunta.
stages.reception: Early printed witness of the Dominican use.

stages.label: 1933 & 1939 Gillet-era Dominican Missals
stages.date_label: 1933–1939 (two Roman editions under Master General Martin Gillet)
stages.scope: 20th-century pre-conciliar editions of the Dominican Missal incorporating post-Divino Afflatu rubric and sanctoral updates.
stages.witness_label: Missale S. Ordinis Praedicatorum (Rome, 1933 & 1939)
stages.summary: Directly inspected front matter of the 1933 and 1939 Rome editions records Master General Martin Gillet's letters announcing corrected rubrics and an updated sanctoral (with 1939 issued as a smaller augmented edition after the 1938 chapter).

evidence.locus: Title page and Gillet prefatory letter
evidence.claim: Attests the 1933 Rome edition with corrected rubrics and sanctoral.

evidence.locus: PDF pp. 2–5, title and Gillet letter
evidence.claim: Attests the 1939 augmented edition following the 1938 General Chapter.

stages.limitations: Front matter inspected; full body textual delta between 1604, 1933, and 1939 remains uncollated.
stages.reception: Official typical/order-wide Dominican editions for pre-1960 celebration.

stages.label: 1965 Dominican Missal (final pre-conciliar Dominican-rite edition)
stages.scope: Final full Dominican-rite altar missal, incorporating 1960–1965 Sacred Congregation of Rites rubric, calendar, and Order adjustments.
stages.witness_label: Missale S. Ordinis Praedicatorum (1965; SRC Prot. 55/965)
stages.summary: Directly inspected front matter prints three distinct SRC approvals, culminating in protocol 55/965 (4 May 1965), applying 1960/1961 calendar and rubric reforms and interim 1965 ritual adjustments while preserving the Dominican Rite.

evidence.locus: Title and SRC decrees, especially PDF p. 4 Prot. 55/965
evidence.claim: Documents the 1960, 1961, and 4 May 1965 SRC approvals governing the 1965 Dominican Missal.

stages.limitations: Front-matter decrees inspected; full line-by-line prayer collation against 1933/1939 remains open.
stages.reception: Official Dominican-rite altar missal immediately preceding the 1969 adoption of the Roman Missal.

stages.label: 1312 Sibert de Beka Ordinal (London General Chapter)
stages.date_label: 1312 London General Chapter promulgation (Lambeth MS 193 witness)
stages.scope: Standardized Carmelite liturgical ordinal regulating Mass and Office incipits across the Order.
stages.witness_label: Sibert de Beka Ordinal (Lambeth Palace MS 193; 1312 promulgation)
stages.summary: Inspected scholarship (Boyce 2004, pp. 18–20) documents the 1312 London General Chapter promulgation of Sibert de Beka's Ordinal, codifying the Carmelite adaptation of the Latin Rite of the Holy Sepulchre.

evidence.claim: Documents the 1312 London General Chapter promulgation of Sibert's Ordinal and its Mass/Office incipits.

stages.limitations: An ordinal specifies incipits and ceremonial directions rather than furnishing a complete altar missal text.
stages.reception: Normative order-wide Carmelite regulatory book of the 14th century.

stages.label: 1490 Brescia Carmelite incunable missal

stages.limitations: Provisional stage; original page images and textual comparison against 1574 remain unexamined.

stages.limitations: Bibliographic attestation only; original 1974 volume and Congregation approval decree remain unacquired.

stages.reception: Earliest printed witness of the Carthusian rite.

stages.label: 1517 Lyon Carthusian folio missal (Simon Bevilacqua)
stages.scope: Early 16th-century Lyon printing associated with the Grande Chartreuse.
stages.witness_label: Missale secundum ordinem Carthusiensium (Lyon: Simon Bevilacqua, 1517)
stages.summary: Bibliographic and scholarly literature identifies Simon Bevilacqua's 1517 Lyon folio printing as an early 16th-century Carthusian missal preceding the post-Tridentine 1582–1627 editions.

evidence.locus: Carthusian Rite: editions of the missal
evidence.claim: Notes early 16th-century Lyon printings of the Carthusian missal (1517 Bevilacqua).

stages.limitations: Provisional lead pending direct BnF/USTC record and scan acquisition.
stages.reception: Publication lead only.

stages.label: 1679 Fourvoirie Carthusian Missal (1677 General Chapter / Innocent Le Masson)
stages.scope: Late-17th-century Carthusian Missal printed at Fourvoirie in Savoy under Prior General Innocent Le Masson.
stages.witness_label: Missale Cartusiani Ordinis (Fourvoirie: Louis du Four, 1679; Gallica bpt6k9127828m)
stages.summary: Directly inspected page images of the engraved title plate (canvas f5) and Prior General Innocent Le Masson's prefatory letter (canvas f7) verify the 1677 General Chapter ordinance ordering a new printing due to scarcity of missals and the 1679 Fourvoirie imprint.

evidence.locus: Canvases f5 (title plate) and f7 (Le Masson prefatory letter)
evidence.claim: Verifies the 1677 General Chapter mandate, Le Masson's authority, and the 1679 Fourvoirie imprint.

stages.limitations: Title plate and opening of prefatory letter inspected; body text not collated against 1627 or later editions.
stages.reception: Official order-wide printing ordered by the 1677 General Chapter.

stages.label: 1883 Montreuil-sur-Mer Carthusian Missal (Dom Anselme-Marie Bruniaux)
stages.scope: Late-19th-century Carthusian Missal printed at Notre-Dame-des-Prés (Montreuil-sur-Mer).
stages.witness_label: Missale sacri ordinis Cartusiensis (Montreuil-sur-Mer: Cartusia S. Mariae de Pratis, 1883)
stages.summary: Scholarly bibliography (King 1955; Martin 1913) identifies the 1883 folio Missale sacri ordinis Cartusiensis printed at Montreuil-sur-Mer under Prior General Dom Anselme-Marie Bruniaux as the landmark late-19th-century pre-Vatican II edition.

evidence.claim: Identifies the 1883 Montreuil-sur-Mer / Cartusia S. Mariae de Pratis edition.

stages.limitations: Provisional lead pending direct scan acquisition and collation against 1679 and 1981.
stages.reception: Order-wide late-19th-century edition reported in scholarship.

stages.label: 1981 postconciliar Missale Cartusiense
stages.date_label: 1981 (provisional bibliographic identity; official order confirms recognition without date)
stages.scope: Post-Vatican II reformed Carthusian Latin Missal retaining the distinct Carthusian Rite.
stages.witness_label: Missale Cartusiense (1981)
stages.summary: The Carthusian Order's official website confirms Roman recognition of the reformed Carthusian missal while NBC 1 (p. 162 lead) identifies the 1981 Latin printing (followed by 1982 English and other vernacular expressions).

evidence.claim: Confirms Roman recognition of the reformed Carthusian missal.
Identifies the 1981 Latin Missale Cartusiense.

stages.limitations: Provisional stage pending direct inspection of the 1981 front matter and Roman recognition decree.
stages.reception: Official reformed Carthusian-rite missal; vernacular translations kept separate as expressions.

stages.label: 1150–1175 Premonstratensian manuscript missal (Charleville MS 3)
stages.scope: Early Premonstratensian manuscript missal witness preceding printed editions.
stages.witness_label: Charleville-Mézières BM MS 3 (1150–1175; Usuarium 2246)
stages.summary: Usuarium origin 232 identifies Charleville MS 3 (1150–1175, alongside Laon 226b) as an early medieval witness to the Norbertine Mass book.

evidence.claim: Identifies Charleville MS 3 (1150–1175) as an early Premonstratensian missal.

stages.limitations: Catalogue metadata only; folio-level collation against early Norbertine ordinals and 1510–1578 prints remains open.
stages.reception: Single medieval house witness.

stages.label: c. 1510 Strasbourg and 1530 Paris Premonstratensian prints
stages.scope: Earliest located printed Premonstratensian missals preceding the 1578 Paris printing.
stages.witness_label: Ordo missalis Premonstratensis (Strasbourg, c. 1510) & Missale Praemonstratense (Paris, 1530)
stages.summary: BSB IIIF manifests verify both the c. 1510 Strasbourg printing (588 canvases, GW M24182 / VD16 M 5647, dating conflict 1500–1511 recorded) and the 1530 Paris printing (510 canvases, BSB 2 Liturg. 235 a).

evidence.claim: Verifies the c. 1510 Strasbourg printing, opening incipit, and 1500–1511 dating conflict.
Verifies the 1530 Paris printing (510 canvases).

stages.limitations: Manifest metadata and 1510 incipit verified; body texts uncollated against each other or 1578.
stages.reception: Early printed Norbertine missal witnesses.

stages.label: 1890 Westmalle Premonstratensian Missal (1889 General Chapter)
stages.date_label: 1890 printing (1889 General Chapter mandate under Sigismund Stary; 1900 successor noted)
stages.scope: Late-19th-century restored Premonstratensian Missal printed at Westmalle Abbey.
stages.witness_label: Missale canonicorum Praemonstratensis ordinis (Westmalle, 1890)
stages.summary: Authorized by the 1889 General Chapter under Abbot General Sigismund Stary and printed by the Cistercians of Westmalle Abbey in 1890 (followed by a 1900 printing), bridging the 18th-century editions and the 1936 Mechelen revision.

evidence.claim: Documents the late-19th-century Westmalle Premonstratensian missal printings (1890/1900).

stages.limitations: Provisional lead pending direct inspection of the 1890 and 1900 title pages and prefaces.
stages.reception: Order-wide late-19th-century Norbertine edition reported in scholarship.

stages.label: 1936 Mechelen Premonstratensian Missal (Abbot General Gummarus Crets)
stages.date_label: 1936 printing (2 September 1936 preface following 1934 General Chapter)
stages.scope: 20th-century pre-conciliar edition of the Premonstratensian-rite Missal.
stages.witness_label: Missale Praemonstratense (Mechelen: H. Dessain, 1936)
stages.summary: Directly inspected title (PDF 3) and Abbot General Gummarus Crets's preface dated 2 September 1936 (PDF 4) document publication by authority of the 1934 General Chapter, explicitly reporting added Masses and changes in text and chant.

evidence.claim: Verifies H. Dessain Mechelen 1936 imprint, 1934 chapter mandate, added Masses, and text/chant revisions.

stages.limitations: Exact changed formularies and line-level collation against 1890/1900/1902 predecessors remain open.
stages.reception: Official pre-Vatican II Premonstratensian altar missal.

stages.label: 1481 Missale Benedictinum incunable witness (Usuarium 469)
stages.scope: Early printed Benedictine missal witness recorded in the inspected Usuarium OSB origin table.
stages.witness_label: Missale Benedictinum (1481; Usuarium 469)
stages.summary: Usuarium origin 409 (row 469) documents a 1481 printed Missale Benedictinum, standing as an early printed monastic witness distinct from Bursfelde 1498 and Cluniac books.

evidence.claim: Identifies the 1481 printed Missale Benedictinum.

stages.limitations: Origin table metadata only; printer, specific congregational provenance, and body text remain uninspected.
stages.reception: Single incunable witness; no order-wide uniformity inferred.

stages.label: 1580 Venice Cassinese Congregation Monastic Missal
stages.scope: Post-Tridentine printed monastic missal of the Cassinese Congregation (alias Sanctae Iustinae).
stages.witness_label: Missale monasticum Congregationis Casinensis alias Sanctae Iustinae (Venice, 1580)
stages.summary: Directly inspected title page (PDF p. 5) verifies the 1580 Venice printing for the Cassinese Congregation citing decrees of its general meetings and leadership; distinct from medieval Montecassino house manuscripts.

evidence.claim: Verifies the Venice 1580 imprint for the Cassinese Congregation alias Sanctae Iustinae.

stages.limitations: Title page only; congregational decrees and textual delta against the 1570 Roman Missal and earlier Benedictine prints remain uncollated.
stages.reception: Bounded to the Cassinese Congregation of Benedictines.

stages.label: 1937 Missale Romano-Monasticum (5th-edition rubric extract)
stages.date_label: 1937 prefatory letter (24 June) and Ratisbon approval (15 August)
stages.scope: 20th-century Roman-base Benedictine monastic missal rubric and front-matter state.
stages.witness_label: Missale Romano-Monasticum, Editio quinta (1937 dated preliminaries)
stages.summary: Directly inspected 27-page rubric extract verifies the Editio quinta title (PDF p. 1), prefatory letter dated 24 June 1937, and Ratisbon approval dated 15 August 1937 (PDF p. 3).

evidence.claim: Verifies Editio quinta rubric title, 24 June 1937 prefatory letter, and 15 August 1937 Ratisbon approval.

stages.limitations: Rubric/front-matter extract only; complete missal text and congregation-level adoption remain unverified.
stages.reception: Roman-base monastic missal preliminaries for Benedictine use.

stages.label: 1965 pre-conciliar OSA Proprium Officiorum et Missarum
stages.scope: Pre-Vatican II updated Augustinian proper attested via official OAD extension rescript.
stages.witness_label: OSA Proprium Officiorum et Missarum (attested 17 July 1965)
stages.summary: Directly inspected 17 July 1965 rescript in Analecta Ordinis OAD authorizes Discalced Augustinians to use the recently approved OSA Office and Mass proper with OAD variations.

evidence.claim: Attests the recently approved OSA Mass/Office proper and authorizes OAD adoption with local variations.

stages.limitations: Attested indirectly through the OAD rescript; primary OSA approval act and complete Latin Mass proper remain unacquired.
stages.reception: Approved OSA proper extended by rescript to OAD.

stages.label: 2006 shared Augustinian Latin Proprium Missarum (OSA/OAR/OAD)
stages.date_label: 17 February 2006 (OAR confirmation; separate decrees for OSA & OAD)
stages.scope: Postconciliar shared Latin Mass proper jointly prepared for the Augustinian family (OSA, OAR, OAD).
stages.witness_label: Shared Augustinian Latin Proprium Missarum (confirmed 17 February 2006)
stages.summary: Directly inspected Acta OAR 2007 (PDF pp. 19–20) prints the 17 February 2006 confirmation of the joint Latin Proprium Missarum sent separately to OSA, OAR, and OAD, tracing the postconciliar revision from 1970 and the 1976 Rome missal.

evidence.claim: Prints the 17 February 2006 confirmation and traces the 1970–1976 postconciliar revision leading to the shared OSA/OAR/OAD Latin proper.

stages.limitations: Acta report inspected; complete 2006 Latin proper text and separate OSA/OAD confirmation decrees remain unacquired.
stages.reception: Shared postconciliar Augustinian-family proper supplementing the Roman Missal.

stages.label: 1998 Servite Proprium Missarum editio typica altera
stages.scope: Second postconciliar typical edition of the Servite proper missal (Antiphonale Sacramentarium and Lectionarium).
stages.witness_label: Servite Proprium Missarum editio typica altera (1998, Vols. I–II)
stages.summary: Both Baroffio's AMEN AMEN (PDF p. 230) and the Servite Order bibliography (p. 585) document the 1998 two-volume editio typica altera (Vol. I Antiphonale Sacramentarium; Vol. II Lectionarium) succeeding the 1972 first typical edition.

evidence.claim: Explicitly names Vol. I Antiphonale Sacramentarium and Vol. II Lectionarium of the 1998 editio typica altera.

evidence.locus: Printed p. 585, Libri Liturgici OSM items 1, 2, 9
evidence.claim: Lists the 1972 volumes and the 1998 second typical edition.

stages.limitations: Bibliographic records inspected; original 1998 front matter, Congregation decree, and exact changes from 1972 remain uncollated.
stages.reception: Second postconciliar typical proper edition for the Order of Servants of Mary.

stages.label: 1223/1230 Reconstructed Franciscan Regula curial missal
stages.scope: Scholarly reconstruction of the early Franciscan missal adopting the Roman Curia's liturgy per the 1223 Regula bullata.
stages.witness_label: Reconstructed Franciscan Regula curial missal (1223/1230)
stages.summary: Inspected scholarship (Welch 2011, pp. 53–61) documents the reconstructed Regula curial missal prototypes mediating the Innocent III / Honorius III papal-chapel liturgy to the Friars Minor prior to Haymo of Faversham.

evidence.claim: Analyzes the reconstructed 1223/1230 Franciscan Regula missal prototypes and distinguishes reconstruction from surviving copies.

stages.limitations: Scholarly reconstruction rather than a located physical archetype; no uniform order-wide edition existed before Haymo.
stages.reception: Early Franciscan reception of the Roman curial liturgy; varied across provinces.

stages.label: Pre-Haymonian Franciscan-curial missal (Assisi MS 607 base hand)
stages.scope: Surviving pre-Haymonian Franciscan-curial missal witness preserving Innocent III-derived rubrics and the Anthony In medio Mass.
stages.witness_label: Assisi, Biblioteca Comunale MS 607 (base hand)
stages.summary: Inspected paleographical analysis (Sedda 2019, pp. 298–319) shows Assisi MS 607's base scribe writing pre-Haymonian curial rubrics adapted for the friars alongside Anthony Mass scheme II (In medio ecclesie) and an added Dominic Mass on f. 79.

evidence.claim: Dates the base sanctorale after 1228–1234 and before Haymo's correction, describing its pre-Haymonian Innocent III rubrics and Anthony In medio formulary.
Contextualizes Assisi 607 within second-quarter 13th-century pre-Haymonian Franciscan missals.

stages.limitations: Scholarly description inspected; full original folio images of Assisi MS 607 not separately acquired.
stages.reception: Concrete pre-Haymonian witness showing practical Franciscan liturgical diversity before 1244.

stages.label: Post-1244 Haymonian correction layer in Assisi MS 607 (hand A2)
stages.date_label: After 1244 (second hand A2 conforming book to Haymo's Ordo; upper bound undated)
stages.scope: Physical marginal and interlinear revision layer conforming an older Franciscan-curial missal to Haymo of Faversham's 1243–1244 Ordo.
stages.witness_label: Assisi, Biblioteca Comunale MS 607 (second hand A2 correction layer)
stages.summary: Sedda 2019 (pp. 315–317 & n. 43) documents a second scribe (A2) systematically inserting Haymo's Ordo rubrics and changed oration incipits in the margins while striking older readings, including entering the Haymonian Anthony Mass on f. 58v.

evidence.claim: Documents hand A2's systematic marginal addition of Haymo's rubrics, altered oration incipits, and the Haymonian Anthony Mass on f. 58v.

stages.limitations: Correcting hand A2 is undated beyond terminus post quem 1244; full manuscript foliation not acquired.
stages.reception: Direct material testimony to how existing Franciscan books were physically updated to Haymo's Ordo.

stages.label: 1263–1280 Nicholas III / Orsini unification of Roman urban books with curial-Franciscan books
stages.date_label: 1263–1280 (John Cajetan Orsini cardinal-protectorate and pontificate as Nicholas III)
stages.scope: Papal-curial liturgical reform harmonizing Roman basilica/urban churches with the modernized curial-Franciscan books.
stages.witness_label: Nicholas III / John Cajetan Orsini curial-Roman reform (1263–1280)
stages.summary: Sedda 2019 (p. 326, synthesizing van Dijk and Cambell) summarizes Orsini/Nicholas III's unification of Roman urban churches with the papal curia, including calendar renewal adding Minorite saints, square notation, and adoption of modernized curial-Franciscan books.

evidence.claim: Reports Orsini/Nicholas III's unification of Roman urban uses with the curia, calendar additions, square notation, and Franciscan-curial book reception.

stages.limitations: Secondary scholarly synthesis; primary bull/ordinal decrees and specific urban Roman basilica reception pace require dedicated manuscript review.
stages.reception: Key bridge transforming the papal-Franciscan curial missal into the standard Roman urban missal.

stages.label: 1482 Venice Roman-curial missal revised by Philip de Rotingo OFM Obs.
stages.scope: Late-15th-century printed Roman-curial missal edited by an Observant Franciscan friar.
stages.witness_label: Missale secundum morem Romanae ecclesiae (Venice: Octavianus Scotus, 1482; ed. Philip de Rotingo OFM Obs.)
stages.summary: Usuarium origin 407 (item 5840, BnF B-27921 fragmentary) documents Octavianus Scotus's 1482 Venetian Roman-curial missal purged of errors by Philip de Rotingo of Mantua OFM Obs., illustrating Observant Franciscan editorial stewardship of the printed Roman Missal.

evidence.claim: Identifies the 1482 Venice Scotus Roman missal revised by Philip de Rotingo OFM Obs.

stages.limitations: Fragmentary copy and catalogue metadata only; edited Roman-curial book, not a distinct Franciscan rite.
stages.reception: Witness to late-15th-century Franciscan editing of the printed Missale Romanum.

transitions.summary: Early Venetian printed Dominican missal succeeds the 13th-century Humbert prototype within the same order use; direct exemplar path unestablished.

evidence.claim: Establishes the 1256 Humbert prototype structure.
Declares Dominican order use in the 1484 Venice printing.

transitions.limitations: Does not claim 1484 was typeset directly from Santa Sabina XIV L 1 or BL Add. MS 23935; intervening 14th–15th-century additions remain uncollated.

transitions.summary: The 1550 Venetian Giunta Dominican missal succeeds the 1484 Nicolaus de Frankfordia printing within the Venetian Dominican printing sequence.

evidence.claim: Establishes the earlier 1484 Venetian Dominican print preceding 1550 Giunta.

transitions.limitations: Bibliographic chronological succession only; textual collation between 1484 and 1550 remains open.

transitions.summary: The 1933/1939 Gillet-era editions succeed earlier post-Tridentine Dominican missals with updated rubrics and sanctoral; intermediate 17th–19th-century editions are unmodeled here.

evidence.claim: Names the 1933 corrected Dominican missal.
Documents the 1939 smaller augmented edition after the 1938 chapter.

transitions.limitations: Multiple intervening Dominican missals (e.g., 1644, 1748, 1855, 1923) are not yet modeled as separate stages.

transitions.summary: The 1965 Dominican Missal revises the 1933/1939 rubrical and calendar framework under the 1960, 1961, and 4 May 1965 SRC approval decrees.

changes.before: 1933/1939 Gillet-era Dominican rubrics prior to the 1960 Code of Rubrics and 1965 interim Order adjustments.
changes.after: Rubrics revised under SRC decrees of 1960, 1961, and Prot. 55/965 (4 May 1965).
changes.locus_before: M33.pdf title and Gillet letter; M39.pdf pp. 2–5
changes.locus_after: M65.pdf front matter and PDF p. 4, SRC Prot. 55/965 (4 May 1965)

evidence.claim: Establishes the pre-1960 rubric state.
Documents the 1960/1961/1965 SRC rubric approvals.

changes.before: 1933/1939 Gillet-era Dominican sanctoral prior to the 1960–1961 calendar simplification.
changes.after: Calendar adapted under the 1960 and 1961 SRC decrees printed in the 1965 front matter.

evidence.claim: Establishes the 1933 sanctoral baseline.
Attests the separate 1960 and 1961 calendar/rubric approvals.
Identifies the earlier 1933 state.
Documents the 1960/1961/1965 approvals governing the 1965 revision.

transitions.limitations: Primary front-matter decree description only; line-by-line collation of individual rubric paragraphs and prayer texts remains open.

transitions.summary: Following CD 98/69 (2 June 1969), the Order transitions from a standalone full Dominican-rite altar missal (1965) to the postconciliar Roman Missal supplemented by the 1985 Dominican Missale et Lectionarium proper.

changes.before: Full Dominican-rite Missal (1965) with distinct Dominican Ordinary and rubrics.
changes.after: Postconciliar Roman Missal adopted as base book under CD 98/69 (2 June 1969), accompanied by a Dominican proper and lectionary (1985).

evidence.claim: Documents the full 1965 Dominican-rite missal.
Cites CD 98/69 adopting the reformed Roman Missal.
Establishes the 1965 full-rite state.
Documents the 1969 Roman-Missal reception and 1985 proper package.

transitions.limitations: Original 1969 decree document itself not separately acquired; subsequent local indult uses of the traditional Dominican Rite are outside this transition.

transitions.summary: The 1574 Venice Carmelite missal stands downstream of the 1312 Sibert de Beka Ordinal within the Holy Sepulchre-derived Carmelite liturgical tradition.

evidence.claim: Documents the 1312 Sibert Ordinal as the normative baseline of the medieval Carmelite liturgy.

transitions.limitations: Bridges 262 years with uncollated incunable intermediates (including Brescia 1490); no direct textual copying asserted.

transitions.summary: The 1935 Rome O.Carm. missal succeeds earlier post-Tridentine Carmelite-rite printings within the Ancient Observance rite.

evidence.claim: Identifies the 1935 Rome Carmelite missal.

transitions.limitations: Bibliographic succession only; intermediate 17th–19th-century printings and full textual changes uncollated.

transitions.summary: The 1974 O.Carm. Proprium Missarum & Lectionarium succeeds the 1935 standalone Carmelite-rite missal as a postconciliar proper volume.

evidence.claim: Identifies the 1935 full Carmelite missal.
Identifies the 1974 postconciliar proper and lectionary.

transitions.limitations: Bibliographic attestation only; the formal postconciliar adoption act transitioning O.Carm. to the Roman Missal base remains to be acquired.

transitions.summary: The 1496 Speyer incunable succeeds medieval manuscript Carthusian missals (such as Charleville MS 154) within the Carthusian Order's use.

evidence.claim: Lists both Charleville MS 154 and the 1496 print under Carthusian use.
Verifies the 1496 Speyer printed missal.

transitions.limitations: Bibliographic succession only; no manuscript-to-print textual collation performed.

transitions.summary: The 1582 post-Tridentine Carthusian Ordinarium succeeds earlier printed Carthusian witnesses including Speyer 1496.

evidence.claim: Verifies the 1496 Speyer printing preceding 1582.

transitions.limitations: Intermediate early-16th-century editions (e.g., 1509, 1517 Lyon, 1561) require direct inspection.

transitions.summary: The 1679 Fourvoirie missal ordered by the 1677 General Chapter under Innocent Le Masson succeeds the 1627 Lyon missal ordered by the 1622 chapter.

evidence.claim: Documents the 1677 General Chapter ordinance and 1679 Fourvoirie imprint.

transitions.limitations: Inspected title plate and prefatory letter do not explicitly cite 1627; body-text changes between 1627 and 1679 remain uncollated.

transitions.summary: The 2021 Missale Cartusiense stands in the same Carthusian-rite line downstream of 1679 (with 1883 and 1981 intermediates provisional pending direct acquisition).

evidence.claim: Documents the 1679 Carthusian missal.
Documents the 2021 Carthusian missal.

transitions.limitations: Intervening 18th–20th-century editions (1713, 1883 Montreuil, 1981) require direct collation to pinpoint when individual textual changes entered.

transitions.summary: Provisional revision edge linking the postconciliar 1981 Carthusian Missal to the 2021 edition, whose inspected Praenotanda §2 explicitly reports revised prayers, prefaces, commons, and ritual order.

changes.before: Postconciliar 1981 Missale Cartusiense state (front matter not yet acquired).
changes.after: 2021 Missale Cartusiense reporting revised prayers, prefaces, and commons.

evidence.claim: Explicitly reports changed prayers, prefaces, commons, and ritual order in the 2021 edition.
Documents the 2021 revisions.

transitions.limitations: Provisional because the 1981 Latin edition itself has not yet been directly acquired and collated against 2021.

transitions.summary: Early Strasbourg (c. 1510) and Paris (1530) prints succeed medieval Premonstratensian manuscript missals such as Charleville MS 3.

evidence.claim: Lists Charleville MS 3 and early printed Premonstratensian missals.
Verifies the c. 1510 Strasbourg printed witness.

transitions.limitations: Bibliographic succession only; body text uncollated.

transitions.summary: The 1578 Paris Premonstratensian missal succeeds the c. 1510 Strasbourg and 1530 Paris printings.

evidence.claim: Verifies the 1530 Paris printing preceding 1578.

transitions.limitations: Bibliographic succession only; no direct typesetting or textual descent asserted.

transitions.summary: The 1936 Mechelen Premonstratensian Missal succeeds the early modern printed Norbertine sequence (with 1739 and 1890/1900 Westmalle printings intervening).

evidence.claim: Verifies the 1936 Dessain printing authorized by the 1934 General Chapter.

transitions.limitations: Multiple intervening printings (1739, 1890, 1900/1902) sit between 1663 and 1936.

transitions.summary: Provisional revision edge from the late-19th-century Westmalle printing to the 1936 Mechelen Missale Praemonstratense, whose inspected preface states that the new book adds Masses and introduces text and chant changes.

changes.before: Late-19th-century Westmalle Premonstratensian missal state (1890/1900, original unacquired).
changes.after: 1936 Mechelen missal adding new Masses and text/chant revisions per Abbot General Gummarus Crets's preface.

evidence.claim: Explicitly states the 1936 book adds Masses and changes in text and chant.
Documents the 1934 chapter mandate and added Masses / text-chant changes.

transitions.limitations: Provisional because the 1890 and 1900/1902 Westmalle predecessors have not yet been directly collated against 1936.

transitions.summary: Chronological succession within Benedictine monastic missal printings from a 1481 incunable witness to the 1580 Cassinese Congregation edition; no congregational identity or textual descent asserted.

evidence.claim: Identifies the 1481 Missale Benedictinum.
Verifies the 1580 Venice Cassinese Congregation missal.

transitions.limitations: Distinct Benedictine congregations maintained separate customs; chronological succession does not assert shared provenance.

transitions.summary: The late-15th-century printed OSA missal succeeds the 14th-century manuscript Ordo missalis (BAV Pal. lat. 500) within the Augustinian Hermits' liturgical stream.

evidence.claim: Identifies the 14th-century Augustinian Ordo missalis.

transitions.limitations: Bibliographic succession only; no direct collation of Pal. lat. 500 against the 1491/1496 printing.

transitions.summary: Between the 1965 pre-conciliar OSA proper and the 2006 shared Latin Proprium Missarum, the Augustinian orders carried out a postconciliar revision (begun 1970, Rome missal 1976) culminating in a unified OSA/OAR/OAD Latin proper confirmed 17 February 2006.

changes.before: 1965 pre-conciliar OSA Proprium Officiorum et Missarum (extended to OAD with separate variations).
changes.after: Postconciliar shared Latin Proprium Missarum prepared jointly for OSA, OAR, and OAD and confirmed 17 February 2006.
changes.locus_before: Analecta Ordinis OAD 1965 vol. 2, 17 July 1965 rescript
changes.locus_after: Acta OAR 2007, PDF pp. 19–20 (17 February 2006 confirmation)

Documents the 1970–1976 postconciliar reform and 2006 unified OSA/OAR/OAD Latin proper.
Attests the 1965 pre-conciliar proper.
Attests the postconciliar revision and 2006 shared Latin proper.

transitions.limitations: Primary institutional decrees inspected; complete Latin prayer texts of both 1965 and 2006 remain unacquired.

transitions.summary: The 1998 two-volume Servite editio typica altera (Antiphonale Sacramentarium and Lectionarium) succeeds the 1972 first typical edition.

evidence.claim: Identifies both volumes of the 1998 editio typica altera following 1972.
Lists the 1972 and 1998 Servite typical editions in sequence.

transitions.limitations: Exact textual and musical revisions between 1972 and 1998 remain uncollated pending acquisition of the 1998 volumes.

transitions.summary: Assisi MS 607's base layer receives the early pre-Haymonian Franciscan adaptation of the Roman curial missal associated with the 1223 Regula bullata.

evidence.claim: Connects early second-quarter 13th-century Franciscan missals to the reconstructed Regula prototype.
Identifies Assisi 607's base layer as pre-Haymonian Innocent III curial ordo adapted for the friars.

transitions.limitations: Regula prototype is a scholarly reconstruction; no single surviving physical exemplar is claimed as Assisi 607's direct antigraph.

transitions.summary: A second hand (A2) physically revises Assisi MS 607 after 1244 to conform its rubrics, prayer incipits, and Anthony Mass to Haymo of Faversham's Ordo.

changes.before: Pre-Haymonian rubrics following Innocent III's curial ordo adapted for the Friars Minor.
changes.after: Haymo of Faversham's post-1244 Ordo rubrics systematically entered in the margins while striking obsolete directions.
changes.locus_after: Sedda 2019, pp. 315, 317 and n. 43 (Assisi MS 607 hand A2)

evidence.claim: Documents hand A2's systematic marginal replacement of pre-Haymonian rubrics with Haymo's Ordo rubrics.

changes.before: Anthony Mass scheme II (In medio ecclesie) and older oration incipits in the base hand.
changes.after: Changed oration incipits and the Haymonian Anthony Mass entered in the margin of f. 58v by hand A2.
changes.locus_after: Sedda 2019, p. 317 and n. 43 (Assisi MS 607 f. 58v margin)

evidence.claim: Documents hand A2 adding changed oration incipits and the Haymonian Anthony Mass on f. 58v.
Paleographical proof of in-codex Haymonian revision of Assisi MS 607.

transitions.limitations: Based on inspected scholarly paleography (Sedda 2019); direct digital folio images of Assisi MS 607 remain to be acquired.

transitions.summary: The Haymonian Franciscan-curial liturgical books are received and extended to the Roman urban churches under Cardinal Orsini / Pope Nicholas III (1263–1280).

evidence.claim: Synthesizes van Dijk and Cambell on Nicholas III's imposition of modernized Franciscan-curial books on the Roman churches.

transitions.limitations: Scholarly synthesis; individual Roman basilica adoption chronologies varied.

transitions.summary: Octavianus Scotus's 1482 Venetian Roman-curial missal (revised by Philip de Rotingo OFM Obs.) succeeds the 1474 Milan editio princeps within the printed Roman-curial tradition.

evidence.claim: Identifies the 1482 Venice Scotus Roman-curial printing edited by Philip de Rotingo.

transitions.limitations: Bibliographic succession only; textual collation against Milan 1474 has not been performed.

gaps.period: Direct inspection of 1486 Brandis, USTC 741258/676212 reconciliation for c. 1505, and 1531 Reformation closure
gaps.missing: Direct acquisition of Usuarium 41 / ISTC im00659300 (Brandis 1486) and reconciliation of c. 1505 USTC 741258 vs 676212, plus Bugenhagen's 1531 Lübeck Church Order marking local cessation of the Catholic diocesan missal.
gaps.next_source: KB København Inc. Haun. 2772 fol. / SB Lübeck I.-K. 877 and USTC 741258/676212 catalogue entries.
gaps.consequence: Neither the relation between 1486 and c. 1505 nor the exact edition identity of c. 1505 is yet settled.

gaps.period: Direct inspection of 1502 UB Leipzig III/243 (Melchior Lotter) and Reformation cessation
gaps.missing: Visual inspection of the 1502 Merseburg missal's prefatory mandate (Ex quo missalium diversitas...) and Mass body, plus mid-16th-century Saxon Reformation closure.
gaps.next_source: UB Leipzig III/243 digital catalogue / VD16 record for Melchior Lotter's 1502 Merseburg missal.
gaps.consequence: Cannot treat the opening incipit as a verified episcopal decree or collate Merseburg's liturgical text against neighboring Magdeburg/Meissen uses.

gaps.period: Pre-1481 monastic manuscripts, Cassinese 1580 body collation, Maurist/Solesmes/Beuron congregational missals, and post-Vatican II Benedictine propers
gaps.missing: Collation of the 1481 incunable and 1580 Cassinese body text against the 1570 Roman Missal, full acquisition of a complete 20th-century Missale Romano-Monasticum (beyond the 1937 27-page rubric extract), and post-1969 Benedictine Confederation proper missals.
gaps.next_source: Complete scans of Cassinese 1580 body, 19th–20th-century Mechlin/Ratisbon/Tournai Missale Romano-Monasticum, and post-1970 Thesaurus Liturgiae Benedictinae.
gaps.consequence: Benedictine monastic liturgy remains sampled at three bounded stations rather than mapped across all autonomous congregations.

gaps.period: 1482 Scotus direct inspection, 1604–1933 intermediate editions, and 1969 CD 98/69 primary decree
gaps.missing: Direct scan of Octavianus Scotus 1482 (ISTC im00636000), key 17th–19th-century editions (e.g., 1644, 1748, 1855, 1923), and the primary text of CD 98/69 (2 June 1969).
gaps.next_source: ISTC im00636000 holdings, BnF/BSB intermediate Dominican missals, and Notitiae 1969/1970 decree notices.
gaps.consequence: Leaves a three-century gap between 1604 and 1933 and keeps 1482 Scotus provisional.

gaps.period: 1490 Brescia scan, 1621–1935 editions, 1935 vs 1937 resolution, and post-1969 O.Carm. reception act
gaps.missing: Page inspection of Gallica bpt6k5578012t (1490 Brescia), 17th–19th-century O.Carm. editions, primary title of 1935 Rome (resolving 1937 report), and primary Congregation decree for 1974 Proprium Missarum.
gaps.next_source: Gallica bpt6k5578012t, Analecta Ordinis Carmelitarum (1935–1937 and 1969–1974), and the 1974 typical edition.
gaps.consequence: Concrete textual revisions between 1621, 1935, and 1974 cannot yet be documented.

gaps.period: 1517 Lyon, 1713 Correria, 1883 Montreuil, and 1981 Latin Missale Cartusiense primary inspections
gaps.missing: Direct page acquisition and collation of Bevilacqua 1517, 1883 Montreuil-sur-Mer, and the 1981 postconciliar Latin edition (plus exact date of Holy See recognition for 1981 and 2021).
gaps.next_source: BnF 1517 Carthusian missal, Montreuil 1883 digitized copy, and primary 1981 Latin Missale Cartusiense front matter.
gaps.consequence: Keeps 1517, 1883, and 1981 provisional and prevents exact textual collation of the 1981→2021 changes reported in Praenotanda §2.

gaps.period: 1890/1900 Westmalle primary scans, 1936 exact delta, and post-Vatican II Norbertine proper
gaps.missing: Direct acquisition of the 1890 and 1900 Westmalle printings to verify the 1936 preface's reported text/chant changes, plus post-1969 Premonstratensian adoption of the Roman Missal and proper volumes.
gaps.next_source: Westmalle 1890/1900 copies in Norbertine abbey libraries (Averbode/Tongerlo/Berne) and post-1970 Analecta Praemonstratensia liturgical decrees.
gaps.consequence: Keeps 1890 Westmalle provisional and leaves post-1969 Norbertine liturgical books unmodeled.

gaps.period: 1491/1496 vs Pal. lat. 500 collation, 1965 OSA original act, and 2006 full Latin proper text
gaps.missing: Folio comparison of BAV Pal. lat. 500 against early printed OSA missals, primary 1965 OSA approval decree, and full 2006 shared OSA/OAR/OAD Latin Proprium Missarum text.
gaps.next_source: BAV Pal. lat. 500 full folios, Analecta Augustiniana (1965), and the published 2006 Latin Proprium Missarum.
gaps.consequence: Concrete prayer-level changes across medieval, 1965, and 2006 Augustinian propers remain uncollated.

gaps.period: 15th–19th-century printed Servite propers and 1998 editio typica altera primary volumes
gaps.missing: Direct acquisition of early modern Servite propers and the 1998 two-volume editio typica altera (Vol. I Antiphonale Sacramentarium, Vol. II Lectionarium) with its Congregation confirmation decree.
gaps.next_source: Curia Generalizia OSM Rome liturgical publications (Libri Liturgici OSM 1–2 bis, 1998).
gaps.consequence: Substantive prayer and chant revisions between 1972 and 1998 cannot yet be verified.

gaps.period: Assisi MS 607 direct folio images, 1280–1474 urban-curial manuscripts, and 1474 vs 1482 Scotus collation
gaps.missing: Digital folios of Assisi MS 607 (especially f. 58v and f. 79), primary curial missals of the Avignon and early Renaissance papacy, and collation of Milan 1474 against Venice 1482 (Philip de Rotingo).
gaps.next_source: Assisi Biblioteca Comunale MS 607 digitization, BnF B-27921 (1482 Scotus), and van Dijk Sources I–II critical apparatus.
gaps.consequence: Prevents direct text-collated verification of Haymo's marginal edits and Philip de Rotingo's 1482 editorial corrections.
